Subject: Sharp p95 + decode errors after modelpack v4-quant deploy (HighNote)

Aditya / Marissa —

We pushed your v4-quant modelpack at 08:00 PT for a blue/green cutover and immediately started seeing p95 jump from ~180ms to ~590ms and a spike of 5xx decode errors on our production hotpath. Throughput dropped ~28% as clients retried. This is affecting critical user flows.

Attached is a small sample of hotpath traces and the error corpus (hotpath-logs.tar.gz). We rolled back on our side for the blue pool but the green pool is still routing some traffic and we're seeing continuing failures.

Can you confirm whether the new qprofile or the model variant could explain the increased decode latency and 5xxs? We need an ETA on a mitigation (rollback or patch). Our CTO Samir is monitoring this and asked for an exec-level update if this isn't resolved in 2 hours.

Thank you — this is high priority for us.

Leah
Leah Moreno
Head of Product Ops, HighNote

Subject: Re: Sharp p95 + decode errors after modelpack v4-quant deploy (HighNote)

Aditya / Leah / Rishi —

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the runtime side after a 20-minute ingest of the traces Leah attached:
- The v4-quant variant introduced a denser int8 kernel path that in many short-sequence requests increases per-token decode CPU on the host (we're seeing increased kernel-switch overhead).
- There are particular request shapes in the sample_requests.txt (mainly a narrow set of prompts with long prefix + streaming calls) that exacerbate KV cache misses and force repeated re-warm of attention caches.
- 5xxs correlate with an upstream decode timeout where our token streamer exceeded the client's configured deadline; in several samples we see transient OOMs on the decoder worker that trigger a 5xx.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Stop routing new traffic to the v4-quant green pool and route all production traffic to the rolled-back variant (we can do this in the control plane now).
2) If rollback isn't acceptable, we can push a targeted qprofile tweak that disables the aggressive kernel switch for short-seq streaming requests (fast path) which should recover p95 within ~15-30m.
3) Enable a temporary longer decoder deadline (increase from 4s -> 8s) to reduce 5xx surface while we stabilize.

I'll prepare a short qprofile diff and a patch for operator-side rollout.

-M

Marissa Cole
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
